message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. A few years ago, I was renting a place with this dude. We were on a lease, which means we had a legal agreement to rent the place for a certain period. When the lease was almost up, he just left without giving much notice. He took most of his stuff, but left a few things and a note saying he didn't want to bring those things with him. Now, where I live, if you don't get rid of your stuff when you move out, the landlord can pay someone to remove it, and they can take money from your deposit for that. I've heard of people losing $250 just because someone had to take three milk crates of their stuff to the dump. That's a rip-off! So, I tried to contact him for two weeks, texting and emailing, asking him to pick up his stuff or take them to the dump. But he never responded. I ended up taking most of his stuff to the dump, but he had around 60 video games for the PS4. I thought, "Why not sell them?" There's a local game store that buys used games, and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Fast forward to last week, I was at a party where he was also there. We were being polite, but then he asked how the move-out process went. I told him it was good, and naturally, he asked what I did with his stuff. When he found out I sold his games, he got mad. I told him I tried to get him to grab those things, but he never reached out. Now he's calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked, and legally, there's nothing wrong with what I did. But now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this. Okay, so to figure this out, I need to think about the different aspects of the situation. First, there's the legal aspect. I know that legally, I didn't do anything wrong because I tried to contact him, and he didn't respond. The landlord can charge for removal, and I followed that process. Selling the games seems like a reasonable thing to do since I couldn't reach him. But then there's the moral aspect. Did I do the right thing by selling his games without his permission? Even though I tried to contact him, maybe I should have made more effort or found another way to handle his stuff. Maybe I could have stored them somewhere or donated them instead of selling them for money. Also, there's the emotional aspect. He's upset because he feels like I took something that was his without his consent. Even if legally I was in the right, emotionally, he feels wronged. That's important because relationships matter, and being labeled an asshole can strain that relationship. Another thing to consider is the value of the games. He had around 60 PS4 games, and I sold them for $600. That's $10 per game on average. Is that a fair price? Did I get a good deal, or could I have sold them for more? If I undercharged, maybe that's part of why he's upset. Also, did I consider his feelings when I sold the games? Maybe I should have thought about how he would feel if he found out his stuff was sold without his input. Even if legally it's fine, emotionally, it's a different story. I also need to think about the communication aspect. I tried to contact him for two weeks, but maybe my methods weren't effective. Did I try calling him? Did I leave messages? Maybe I should have escalated my efforts to ensure he was aware of the situation. Furthermore, there's the aspect of the rip-off with the landlord. I know that not dealing with the stuff can cost money, but did I explain that to him when I tried to contact him? Maybe he didn't realize the potential financial loss if he didn't respond. Lastly, there's the question of whether I should offer him some of the money from the sale, even if legally I don't have to. It might help mend the relationship and show that I care about his feelings, even though I was within my rights. So, putting it all together, while I didn't do anything legally wrong, there are several moral and emotional considerations that make me wonder if I'm the asshole in this situation. I need to balance the legal rightness with the emotional impact on our relationship.
